overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the November 9 email memorialized a prior open meeting and was not deliberation, and the AG declined to review the individual-authority allegations.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged two Board members, without authority, directed the administrative assistant to draft and send a November 9 email stating the Board had voted to dissolve a committee.
allegations.key_passage: As a preliminary matter, we decline to review allegations concerning the authority of individual Board members to take action or issue communications or directives, purportedly on behalf of the Board, without a vote of the Board.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged that the November 9 email, sent to a quorum of the Board and others, was deliberation outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the email simply memorialized the discussions that occurred during a prior meeting, and therefore the circulation of the email merely served an administrative purpose similar to circulating draft minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a Board member, without authority, directed local public access television not to release a recording of a November 17 committee meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, these allegations, even if true, would not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law and we decline to review them.
